title: Vintage Gibson SG Custom Value Guide: Pickups And Era
description: Compare vintage SG Custom value by era, finish, original pickups and repairs. Joe explains how three-pickup Customs fit the market before an appraisal.
h1: Vintage Gibson SG Custom Value Guide
alt: Walnut-finish Gibson SG Custom with three covered pickups, gold hardware and a Bigsby vibrato

faqs.q: How Much Is A Vintage Gibson SG Custom Worth?
faqs.a: A played walnut 1968 to 1969 Gibson SG Custom with its original pickups and case falls around $6,500 to $10,500 in the completed-sale comparisons reviewed as of October 2026. This band allows minor wiring changes and localized finish touch-up; I don't use it for an excellent, untouched early Custom.

faqs.q: What Condition Does This Price Range Assume?
faqs.a: Original finish and pickup set with original case; visible wear and minor wiring or hardware changes. Localized finish touch-up allowed. No reported structural break or full refinish. Not an excellent all-original band. I match those details before using the $6,500 to $10,500 range for an individual guitar.

faqs.q: Is A Dealer Offer The Same As The Published Range?
faqs.a: It isn't. The table describes completed-sale comparisons before shipping and tax. A buying offer also accounts for the instrument's condition, selling costs, preparation and the dealer's margin. I explain an offer for the actual guitar rather than promising the top of a general range.

faqs.q: Does A Quality Refret Change The Collector Category?
faqs.a: A quality refret is accepted maintenance and preserves the all-original classification of an otherwise all-original guitar. It takes the instrument out of the museum-quality category. Neck reshaping is a separate alteration.
